title: Maximum Path Score in a Grid
summary: Given an m x n grid with cell values 0, 1, or 2, and an integer k, find the maximum score from (0,0) to (m-1,n-1) by moving right or down, where each cell's value adds to the score and incurs a cost.
statement: Given an m x n grid with cell values 0, 1, or 2, and an integer k, find the maximum score from (0,0) to (m-1,n-1) by moving right or down, where each cell's value adds to the score and incurs a cost. The score must not exceed k, or return -1 if no valid path exists.
constraints: grid has up to 200 rows and columns and values zero, one, or two; its first cell is zero.
Move only right or down; nonzero cells cost one budget unit and contribute their value to score.
Return the maximum score using cost at most k, or negative one when no path fits.
hints: A path state needs its cell, used budget, and best score; worse scores at the same state are dominated.
Sweep the grid and merge states from the top and left, adding the current cell’s cost and score.
Keep the maximum score for each reachable cost no greater than k.
Every monotone path reaches a cell from exactly one predecessor, so the transitions enumerate all feasible paths and retain their optimum.
editorial: Every monotone path reaches a cell from exactly one predecessor, so the transitions enumerate all feasible paths and retain their optimum.
